questions.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium differ by 4 cm. Its height is 8 cm and the area is 192 cm². What are the lengths of the parallel sides?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area = (1 ÷ 2) × (sum of parallel sides) × height

192 = (1 ÷ 2) × (a + b) × 8 ⇒ (a + b) = 48

Given difference: a − b = 4

Use formula: numbers = (sum ± difference) ÷ 2

**∴ Answer = 26 cm and 22 cm**

questions.question: A right prism has a trapezium-shaped base with parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, height of trapezium 5 cm, and prism height 15 cm. Find the volume.

Volume of prism = Base area × height

Base (trapezium) area = (1 ÷ 2) × (6 + 10) × 5 = 40 cm²

Volume = 40 × 15 = 600 cm³

**∴ Answer = 600 cm³**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Parallel sides = 6 cm, 10 cm

Height of trapezium = 5 cm

Height of prism = 15 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of trapezium = (1 ÷ 2) × (a + b) × h

Volume = Base area × prism height

 
 
 
• 
• 
• 
• 10 cm 6 cm 5 cm 15 cm 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of base = (1 ÷ 2) × (6 + 10) × 5

⇒ = (1 ÷ 2) × 16 × 5 = 40 cm²

⇒ Volume = 40 × 15

⇒ Volume = 600 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 600 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Trapezium

questions.question: A cylinder is melted and recast into 8 smaller cylinders of the same height. If the original radius was 6 cm and height 10 cm, find the radius of each small one?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume conserved ⇒ πR²H = 8 × πr²H

Height same ⇒ cancel π and H ⇒ R² = 8r²

r = R ÷ √8 = 6 ÷ (2√2) = 3 ÷ √2

Rationalize ⇒ r = (3√2) ÷ 2

**∴ Answer = (3√2) ÷ 2 cm ≈ 2.12 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original radius R = 6 cm

Height = 10 cm

Number of cylinders = 8

**Formula used:**

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

 R = 6 cm 8 cylinders 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original volume = π × 6² × 10

⇒ = π × 36 × 10 = 360π

⇒ Total volume of 8 cylinders = 8 × π × r² × 10

⇒ 360π = 80πr²

⇒ r² = 360 ÷ 80 = 4.5

⇒ r = √4.5 = (3√2) ÷ 2 = 2.12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2.12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a solid is melted and recast, total volume remains same

Scaling Rule

If number of parts = n and height same, then r ∝ 1 ÷ √n

Cylinder Volume

Volume = π × r² × h

Root Simplification

√4.5 = √(9 ÷ 2) = (3√2) ÷ 2

∠ABP

questions.question:
Consider the following two statements, labeled Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Evaluate them and choose the appropriate answer from the given options.**
Assertion (A):** Two non-intersecting and non-touching circles have four common tangents.**
Reason (R):** Two direct and two transverse tangents can be drawn between such circles.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Non-intersecting & non-touching circles ⇒ separate circles

Such circles have 4 common tangents

2 direct + 2 transverse tangents

Assertion is true, Reason correctly explains it

**∴ Answer = Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two non-intersecting and non-touching circles

**Formula used:**

Number of common tangents depends on position of circles

 
• 
• 
• 
• Direct Tangents Transverse Tangents 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Non-intersecting, non-touching circles ⇒ separate circles

⇒ Number of tangents = 4

⇒ Types: 2 direct + 2 transverse

⇒ Assertion is true

⇒ Reason correctly explains the Assertion

**∴ The correct answer is: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Number of Common Tangents

Separate circles ⇒ 4 tangents, Touch externally ⇒ 3, Intersect ⇒ 2, Touch internally ⇒ 1, One inside another ⇒ 0.

Direct Tangents

Tangents that do not intersect the line joining centers.

Transverse Tangents

Tangents that intersect the line joining centers.

Key Geometry Rule

Always identify relative position of circles to determine number of tangents.

questions.question: If sqrt{x} = 11, what is the value of x + sqrt{x}?
questions.solution:
Here is the HTML output based on the given question: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If √x = 11, then x = 11² = 121.

Now, x + √x = 121 + 11.

∴ Answer = 132

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√x = 11

**Formula used:**

x + √x = x + square root of x

 x = 121 √x = 11 
• x + √x 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = 11² = 121

⇒ x + √x = 121 + 11 = 132

**∴ The correct answer is 132.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root Basics

The square root of a number y is the value which, when squared, gives y. Example: √121 = 11.

Perfect Squares

A perfect square is a number that has an integer as its square root. Example: 121 is a perfect square of 11.

Addition with Square Roots

When adding a square root and its square, compute each separately and then sum. Example: x + √x.

questions.question: Which of the following is a perfect square of an even number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To check if a number is a perfect square of an even number:

1. Verify if the number is a perfect square.

2. Check if the square root of the number is an even integer.

Among the options, 144 is a perfect square (√144 = 12, which is even).

**∴ Answer = 144**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Options: 81, 144, 121, 169

**Formula used:**

Perfect Square of Even Number ⇒ √N = even integer

 81 144 121 169 √144 = 12, Even 

**Calculations:**

⇒ √81 = 9 (odd), not valid

⇒ √144 = 12 (even), valid

⇒ √121 = 11 (odd), not valid

⇒ √169 = 13 (odd), not valid

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares

A number is a perfect square if its square root is an integer, e.g., √144 = 12.

Perfect Square of Odd Numbers

To check for odd numbers, ensure √N = odd integer, e.g., √121 = 11.

Non-Perfect Squares

Numbers like 50 or 75 are not perfect squares as their square roots are not integers.

questions.question: Two numbers 63527 and 60784 are divided by a certain three-digit number and leave the same remainder. What is the sum of digits of the divisor?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

63527

60784

**Formula Used:**

If two numbers leave the same remainder when divided by a number, then their difference is divisible by that number

**Calculation:**

⇒ 63527 − 60784 = 2743

⇒ Divisor must be a factor of 2743

⇒ 2743 = 13 × 211

⇒ Three-digit divisor = 211

⇒ Sum of digits = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

questions.question: Which of the following sets is a proper subset of rational numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Natural numbers (N), Irrational numbers (P), Real numbers (R), and Imaginary numbers (I).

**Definition: **

A rational number (Q) is any number that can be expressed as p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

 Rational Numbers (Q) Integers (Z) Natural Numbers (N) {1, 2, 3, 4, ...} 

⇒ Let n be any natural number, n ∈ {1, 2, 3, ...}.

⇒ n can be written as n/1, which is in the form p/q.

⇒ Since p = n and q = 1 are both integers and 1 ≠ 0, n is a rational number.

⇒ This means N ⊂ Q.

⇒ Also, there exist rational numbers (like 1/2) that are not natural numbers, making N a proper subset.

⇒ Irrational numbers (P) are defined as numbers that are NOT rational (Q ∩ P = φ).

⇒ Real numbers (R) include all rational numbers (Q ⊂ R), so R is a superset, not a subset.

**∴ The correct answer is Natural number.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proper Subset

A set A is a proper subset of B (A ⊂ B) if all elements of A are in B, but there is at least one element in B not in A.

Number System Hierarchy

The relationship is: Natural Numbers (N) ⊂ Whole Numbers (W) ⊂ Integers (Z) ⊂ Rational Numbers (Q) ⊂ Real Numbers (R).

Irrational Numbers

Numbers that cannot be expressed as p/q, such as π, e, or √2. They have non-terminating, non-repeating decimal expansions.

Complex Numbers

The set of all numbers in the form a + bi, where a and b are real and i = √−1. Real numbers are a subset of Complex numbers.

questions.question: A scholarship fund of ₹1200 is to be distributed between two students, A and B, in a ratio 5:3. However, after allocating ₹200 to administrative charges, the remaining amount is first increased by 10% as a bonus before the final division. What amount will student A receive?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net fund = 1200 − 200 = 1000

Increase by 10% ⇒ 1000 × 1.1 = 1100

Ratio 5 : 3 ⇒ A gets 5/8 of total

A's share = 1100 × 5 ÷ 8 = 687.5

**∴ Answer = ₹687.50**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total fund = 1200, Charges = 200, Bonus = 10%, Ratio = 5 : 3

**Formula used:**

Final share = (Remaining amount × (1 + bonus%)) × ratio part ÷ total parts

 ₹1200 − ₹200 +10% Initial Charges Bonus Final = ₹1100 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Remaining = 1200 − 200 = 1000

⇒ After 10% bonus = 1000 + 100 = 1100

⇒ A's share = 1100 × 5 ÷ 8 = 687.5

**∴ The correct answer is ₹687.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Distribution

Share = Total × individual ratio ÷ sum of ratios. Example: A = Total × 5 ÷ (5+3).

Percentage Increase

New value = Original × (1 + rate/100). Example: 1000 × 1.1 = 1100.

Successive Operations

Always apply operations in order: first subtraction, then percentage change.

Unitary Method

Find value of 1 part = Total ÷ sum of ratio, then multiply by required parts.

questions.question: Average score of a batsman in 10 innings is 32. How many runs must he score in the 11th innings to raise his average to 34?
questions.solution:
Here is the solution to the given question, formatted exactly as per the specified rules: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New total runs required = New average × Total innings = 34 × 11 = 374.

Current total runs = Old average × Old innings = 32 × 10 = 320.

Runs needed in 11th innings = New total − Current total = 374 − 320 = 54.

**∴ Answer = 54**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average after 10 innings = 32

New average after 11 innings = 34

**Formula used:**

New total runs = New average × Total innings

Runs in 11th innings = New total − Current total

 Current total = 320 New total = 374 
• Difference = 54 

**Calculations:**

New total runs = 34 × 11 = 374

⇒ Runs in 11th innings = 374 − 320 = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = Total sum ÷ Number of items

Effect of Adding a New Value

Adding a new value changes the average based on how it compares to the previous average.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups, weighted average = (Sum of weighted values) ÷ Total weights.

Deviation Method

Change in average = (Difference in total sum) ÷ Total number of items.

questions.question: Average of 11 numbers is 45. Average of first 5 is 42 and last 5 is 46. Find the 6th number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of all 11 numbers = Average × Count = 45 × 11 = 495

Sum of first 5 numbers = 42 × 5 = 210

Sum of last 5 numbers = 46 × 5 = 230

6th number = Total sum − (Sum of first 5 + Sum of last 5) = 495 − (210 + 230) = 55

**∴ Answer = 55**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 11 numbers = 45

Average of first 5 numbers = 42

Average of last 5 numbers = 46

**Formula used:**

Sum = Average × Count

 
 First 5
 Sum = 210
 
 6th
 ?
 
 Last 5
 Sum = 230
 
• 
 Total Sum = 495

**Calculations:**

Total sum of all 11 numbers = 45 × 11 = 495

Sum of first 5 numbers = 42 × 5 = 210

Sum of last 5 numbers = 46 × 5 = 230

⇒ 6th number = 495 − (210 + 230) = 55

**∴ The correct answer is 55.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When groups have different averages, the combined average is calculated as (Sum of all groups) ÷ (Total number of elements).

Deviation Method

To find a missing number in a group, subtract known sums from the total sum.

Arithmetic Mean

The average or mean of n numbers is the sum of the numbers divided by n: Mean = Sum ÷ Count.

questions.question: A man's salary is increased by 40% and then decreased by 30%. What is the net effect on his salary?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When successive percentages are applied, the net percentage effect = (x + y + xy/100), where x and y are the successive percentage changes.

Here, x = +40% (increase), y = −30% (decrease).

Net effect = 40 − 30 + (40 × −30)/100 = 10 − 12 = −2%.

**∴ Answer = 2% decrease**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Initial increase = 40%, followed by a decrease = 30%.

**Formula used:**

Net percentage effect = (x + y + xy/100).

 Initial Salary = 100 +40% Increase → 140 −30% Decrease → 98 

**Calculations:**

Initial salary = 100 (assume base 100 for simplicity).

⇒ After 40% increase: 100 + 40 = 140.

⇒ After 30% decrease: 140 − (30% of 140) = 140 − 42 = 98.

⇒ Net effect = 100 − 98 = −2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 2% decrease (Option 1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

For successive changes of x% and y%, the net percentage effect = x + y + xy/100.

Order of Changes

The order of increase and decrease matters. Calculate step by step for clarity.

Shortcut for Small Changes

When x and y are small, approximate: Net effect ≈ x + y.

Application in Real Life

Used in salary adjustments, discounts, and profit/loss calculations.

questions.question: A bookstore buys 2,000 books for ₹180 each. They offer a "Buy 4, Get 1 Free" scheme but sell at the marked price of ₹225 per book. What is their effective profit percentage per book sold (after adjusting for the free books)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Buy 4 Get 1 Free ⇒ total 5 books but paid for 4

Effective SP per book = (4 × 225) ÷ 5 = 900 ÷ 5 = 180

CP per book = 180

SP = CP ⇒ No profit, no loss

**∴ Answer = 0%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

CP per book = 180, MP (SP) = 225

Scheme: Buy 4 Get 1 Free ⇒ 5 books given for price of 4

**Formula used:**

Effective SP per book = Total SP ÷ Total books

 225 225 225 225 FREE Pay for 4, get 5 books 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total SP for 5 books = 4 × 225 = 900

⇒ Effective SP per book = 900 ÷ 5 = 180

⇒ CP per book = 180

⇒ Profit = 180 − 180 = 0

⇒ Profit % = 0%

**∴ The correct answer is 0%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free Concept

Discount % = Y ÷ (X + Y) × 100. Here = 1 ÷ 5 × 100 = 20% effective discount.

Effective Selling Price

Effective SP per unit = (Paid units × SP) ÷ Total units received.

Profit Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. If SP = CP, then profit = 0%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Even if MP is high, schemes like free items reduce effective SP, impacting profit.

questions.question: 16 men can complete a work in 15 days. How many men are required to complete the same work in 10 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The work is inversely proportional to the number of men.

Men required = (Initial men × Initial days) ÷ New days

⇒ Men required = (16 × 15) ÷ 10 = 24 men

**∴ Answer = 24 men**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

16 men can complete the work in 15 days. Number of men required to complete the same work in 10 days = ?

**Formula used:**

Men required = (Initial men × Initial days) ÷ New days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Men required = (16 × 15) ÷ 10

⇒ Men required = 240 ÷ 10

⇒ Men required = 24 men

**∴ The correct answer is 24 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality Rule

When two quantities are inversely proportional, the product of the two remains constant. Example: Men × Days = Constant.

Work and Time Relationship

If the amount of work remains constant, increasing the number of workers reduces the required time proportionally.

LCM Method for Work

LCM is often used in work problems to find the total work, especially when multiple workers are involved with different efficiencies.

Efficiency: A = 4, B = 3, C = 2 → Total = 9/day

questions.question: A person lent ₹2,000 at 6% per annum simple interest and ₹3,000 at 5% per annum simple interest. Find his total interest after 3 years.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use I = P × R × T ÷ 100 separately

For ₹2000: I = 2000 × 6 × 3 ÷ 100 = 360

For ₹3000: I = 3000 × 5 × 3 ÷ 100 = 450

Total Interest = 360 + 450 = 810

**∴ Answer = ₹810**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P₁ = 2000, R₁ = 6%, T = 3 years

P₂ = 3000, R₂ = 5%, T = 3 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = P × R × T ÷ 100

 
• ₹2000 @6% ₹3000 @5% Time = 3 years 

**Calculations:**

⇒ I₁ = 2000 × 6 × 3 ÷ 100 = 360

⇒ I₂ = 3000 × 5 × 3 ÷ 100 = 450

⇒ Total Interest = 360 + 450 = 810

**∴ The correct answer is ₹810.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100

Combined Principal Trick

If time is same, find weighted average rate and apply on total principal

Amount Formula

Amount = Principal + Interest

Rate Conversion

Percentage rate means per 100 → always divide by 100 in SI formula

questions.question: If sin²theta = (1 - cos²theta )/(2), what is the value of sin⁴ theta in terms of cos 2theta ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that sin²θ = (1 − cos 2θ) ÷ 2.

Therefore, sin⁴θ = (sin²θ)².

⇒ sin⁴θ = [(1 − cos 2θ) ÷ 2]².

⇒ sin⁴θ = (1 − cos 2θ)² ÷ 4.

**∴ Answer = (1 − cos 2θ)² ÷ 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:**

sin²θ = (1 − cos 2θ) ÷ 2.

**Formula used:**

sin⁴θ = (sin²θ)².

**Calculations:**

sin²θ = (1 − cos 2θ) ÷ 2.

⇒ sin⁴θ = [(1 − cos 2θ) ÷ 2]².

⇒ sin⁴θ = (1 − cos 2θ)² ÷ 4.

**∴ The correct answer is (1 − cos 2θ)² ÷ 4 (Option 1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between sin²θ and cos 2θ

sin²θ = (1 − cos 2θ) ÷ 2 and cos²θ = (1 + cos 2θ) ÷ 2.

Square of sin²θ

sin⁴θ = (sin²θ)² is derived by squaring sin²θ.

Double Angle Formula

cos 2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ or cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1.

Applications in Trigonometry

These formulas are widely used in integration, differentiation, and solving trigonometric equations.

questions.question: Two observers stand 100 meters apart and observe the top of a tower. The angles of elevation are 30° and 45°. Find the height of the tower (assuming both observers are on the same side of the tower).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Closer observer has larger angle = 45°, so height = distance from tower.

Let nearer distance = x ⇒ height = x

Farther distance = x + 100

tan30° = h ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3

x ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3 ⇒ x = 100 ÷ (√3 − 1)

**∴ Answer = 50(√3 + 1) m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between observers = 100 m

Angles of elevation = 30°, 45°

Both on same side of tower

**Formula used:**

tanθ = height ÷ base

 
• 
• h 45° 30° 
• 
• 
• 100 m 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let distance of nearer observer = x

⇒ tan45° = h ÷ x ⇒ 1 = h ÷ x ⇒ h = x

⇒ Distance of farther observer = x + 100

⇒ tan30° = h ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3

⇒ x ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3

⇒ √3x = x + 100 ⇒ x(√3 − 1) = 100

⇒ x = 100 ÷ (√3 − 1) = 50(√3 + 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 50(√3 + 1) m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angles of Elevation Concept

Angle between horizontal and line of sight. tanθ = height ÷ base is most useful relation.

Same Side Observation Rule

Distance difference is directly added: farther distance = nearer distance + separation.

Standard Values

tan30° = 1 ÷ √3, tan45° = 1 — frequently used in height-distance problems.

Rationalization Trick

1 ÷ (√3 − 1) = (√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = (√3 + 1) ÷ 2 for faster simplification.

questions.question: If, x + y = 7 and xy = 10 then the value of x² + y² is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the identity: x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

Given: x + y = 7 and xy = 10

⇒ x² + y² = 7² − 2 × 10

⇒ x² + y² = 49 − 20 = 29

**∴ Answer = 29**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + y = 7 and xy = 10

**Formula used:**

x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

**Calculations:**

⇒ Substitute: x² + y² = (7)² − 2 × 10

⇒ Simplify: x² + y² = 49 − 20 = 29

**∴ The correct answer is 29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Related Identity: Expansion Formula

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

Sum and Product of Roots

For quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, sum of roots = −b/a and product of roots = c/a.

Difference of Squares

x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y)

Useful Identity

x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

questions.question: A man takes a loan of ₹15,000 from a bank at 8% compound interest per annum, compounded annually. Find the total amount he has to pay after 2 years.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use CI multiplying factor: (1 + r/100)t

Here factor = (1.08)² = 1.1664

Amount = 15000 × 1.1664

**∴ Answer = 17496**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal = 15000

Rate = 8% per annum

Time = 2 years

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

 
• Start 1 yr 2 yr 15000 ×1.08 ×1.08 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 15000 × (1 + 8/100)²

⇒ A = 15000 × (1.08)²

⇒ A = 15000 × 1.1664

⇒ A = 17496

**∴ The correct answer is 17496.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

A = P(1 + r/100)t, where interest = A − P.

Successive Multiplication Trick

For multiple years, multiply principal by (1 + r/100) repeatedly.

Difference between SI and CI

CI grows faster as interest is added to principal each year.

Effective Rate Concept

For 2 years, effective increase = (1.08)² − 1 = 16.64%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹450. He marks up its price by 20%. He then offers a discount of 10% on the marked price to a customer. What is the profit percentage the shopkeeper makes on this transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive change: +20% then −10%

Net factor = 1.2 × 0.9 = 1.08

So profit = 8%

**∴ Answer = 8%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price = 450

Markup = 20%

Discount = 10%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + markup) × (1 − discount)

 CP = 450 +20% −10% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = 450 × 1.2 = 540

⇒ SP = 540 × 0.9 = 486

⇒ Profit = 486 − 450 = 36

⇒ Profit% = (36 ÷ 450) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

Net change = a + b + (a × b)/100 for successive % changes.

Markup and Discount Relation

SP = CP × (1 + markup/100) × (1 − discount/100).

When Profit Occurs

If markup% > discount%, then profit; otherwise loss.

Quick Check Trick

1.2 × 0.9 = 1.08 ⇒ 8% gain directly without full calculation.
